_schema: One station, in the shape M3 fixed. M4 adds four fields and every one of them is a station's business rather than a canvas's: span, which is where this station sits in the ten years and is what turns tau into a chronology; pitch and depth on a canvas, which are the two new treatments; and curl, which is how much of the measured motion this station spends.
title: Saint-Remy
_canvases: In the order he painted them: the irises in his first week in the asylum, the night sky in June, the olive grove through June and July. Three canvases and three treatments, and none of the three is the lifted plain of station 4 -- which is the point of building this station second. treatment overrides what tools/place.py measured, and where it does, the reason is here.

canvases.title: Irises
canvases.collection: J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles
canvases.note: Laid flat at 1:1, which is not an override of the measurement but a consequence of it: this canvas scores 1.7x on the level-against-upright cut, the lowest in the whole set and below a self-portrait's 2.6x, so there is no horizon in it and it is not a place. It is a picture of the ground, seen from above, at the size the ground was. He painted it in this garden in his first week here, working from nature, and it is 74.3 by 94.3 cm, so this is where your feet are.

canvases.title: The Starry Night
canvases.collection: Museum of Modern Art, New York
canvases.note: Overhead, and that is a choice with a cost. This canvas measures 2.0x on the horizon test -- the same as a self-portrait, below the 5x that makes a canvas a place -- so its own measured horizon is not worth hanging it by, and it is hung by its middle instead. Tipped up 52 degrees, which is where a viewer lying down looks: from there it is exactly the painting, on the same rays it came off the canvas on, and from standing it is above you and you have to lie down. That is DESIGN 6's whole argument for lying down and it is why this station exists.

canvases.title: Olive Grove
canvases.note: This canvas has the strongest horizon in the whole collection -- 105x the best upright cut, against the Harvest's 72x -- so tools/place.py calls it a plain and it would lift. It is shelled instead, and the reason is the station rather than the canvas: station 8 already has a sky overhead and a ground at its feet, and what it has not got is a middle distance. The measurement is not discarded; the horizon it found is what puts the canvas at eye level.
canvases._depth: DESIGN 15 is right that monocular depth estimation on a Van Gogh is outside the training distribution of anything worth using, so this is a person looking at the canvas and typing metres. u and v are canvas fractions, d is metres from the standpoint along that stroke's own ray, and inverse distance fills in between. The ground rows follow what a plane at 1.65 m of eye height would demand; the trunks and the canopy stand in front of it, which is the whole of what a shell adds over a lift. tools/shell.py then measures where it tears, and that number is not authored.

_ground: The walled garden is flat, and the swell that station 4 has is not here: a plain a mile wide has a swell in it and a garden does not. dome is where the sky is, and it is the same 260 m so that the two stations are lit and scaled the same way.
_volume: Station 4's z half came from where the lifted paint thins to a quarter of its density. A shell has a different and sharper limit and tools/shell.py measures it in closed form: two strokes that are neighbours on the canvas sit on almost the same ray, so stepping sideways by delta opens an angle of delta times the difference of their reciprocal depths, and the paint has torn when that exceeds what a stroke subtends. That number is 2.34 m on this canvas -- a twentieth of the neighbouring pairs have opened a stroke-wide hole by then, a tenth by 3.4 m and a fifth by 5.4 m -- and it is recorded here as tears. The station does not ship at 2.34: a slab that small would put a walking body at its edge every second of the piece, which is the failure DESIGN 15 is actually afraid of. It ships at 9 by 6 with the number beside it, the same bargain station 4 makes and the same instrument running, and the two are meant to be read together: the lifted plain thins to a quarter by 6 m, the shell tears at 2.3, and an ambling body wants fifty.
_weave: Jute. He ran out of canvas at Saint-Remy and Theo's next parcel was slow, so he painted on the coarse sacking cloth that was to hand -- and DESIGN 4.5 is right that it is not fine linen scaled up: its threads vary along their length and it slubs, which is why rough is a separate number from the period. The floor crossfades from station 4's linen to this on the road between them, which is the year it changed in.
_pacing: The same constant as station 4, because DESIGN 5.3's whole argument is that one constant is what makes every relative tempo true.
_curl: DESIGN 4.5's one motion. gain is the fraction of the measured amplitude this station spends -- the amplitude itself is per stroke and packed in the blob, measured by sliding every stroke along its own arc across the scan until the paint under it stopped being a colour it could have been traced from. rate is the invention: there is no time in a painting, and this is the only number here that admits it. 0.42 rad/s is a swing of fifteen seconds.
_letter: To Theo, from the asylum, the week he painted the sky. The text stays null until M7, which owns the voice and the verification against the Van Gogh Museum and Huygens edition.

caption.title: Saint-Remy
caption.sub: The asylum garden, 1889. The sky overhead is a choice and the caption says so: this canvas has no measurable horizon in it -- its best level colour cut beats its best upright one by 2.0x, which is what a self-portrait scores -- so it is hung by its middle and tipped up to where a lying viewer looks. What is measured is the motion. Every stroke was slid along the arc it draws until the paint it landed on stopped being a colour it could have been traced from, and that distance is how far it is allowed to move. Along the mirrored arc it breaks 1.8x sooner, so the curl is real; against a straight slide it barely wins, and a bed of irises wins by more, so the curl is not special to this canvas. The depth in the olive grove is a person typing metres, and the metre it tears at is not.
